test: Run exactly one native Windows App Server session; hold one mock response for a fixed 1.0 s after turn/interrupt is sent; record interrupt send, RPC acknowledgement, client EOF, gate release, and turn/completed using perf_counter_ns and sequence IDs.
isolation: temporary CODEX_HOME; localhost-only Responses mock; API credential env vars removed; read-only thread sandbox; no provider/model/game/GUI/input
decision: PASS_WINDOW_ABORT requires accepted interrupt, one request, HTTP disconnect before fixed gate release, matching turn/completed status interrupted, and no server errors. TIMING_MEASURABLE requires perf_counter resolution <=1 us and timestamps for send, ack, disconnect, and release. Otherwise retain FAIL/STOP/TIMING_UNRESOLVED; no retry.
uncertainty: No latency distribution or SLA inference; no actual provider, game, GUI, OS input, physical release, task feedback, recovery, ammo/progress, or terminal outcome.
hypothesis: Codex CLI 0.160.0 turn/interrupt aborts a held local Responses HTTP request and completes the active turn as interrupted; QueryPerformanceCounter-backed perf_counter can measure request-close and turn-completion timing.
counterevidence: The remote model provider may continue inference/billing after HTTP cancellation; endpoint close does not prove provider work stopped. This is one host/CLI sample only.
